summary: Among the most lethal states on record and institutionally behind its own law: the 2021 national hate-crime count recorded 7 violent deaths of LGBT+ people in the state, whose penal code has recognised anti-trans bias crimes since 2021 (Article 211 Bis reform). Its 2021 civil-code reform created an administrative gender-recognition procedure but excluded under-18s; after the Supreme Court struck that exclusion down in June 2023 the congress had still not complied as of March 2025 - among the clearest legislative non-compliance cases in the country.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (no cached copy); Human Rights Watch report "I Just Want to Contribute to Society" (6 March 2024) on the need for legal gender recognition in Tabasco state - it documents that the absence of any gender-recognition procedure exposes trans people to police and institutional mistreatment, co-authored with a local trans community organisation; the dossier cites it as the clearest case among the six states whose legislatures still refuse any procedure.

Guardian report (24 July 2024) on Mexico City making transfeminicide a crime with sentences of up to 70 years (the 'Paola Buenrostro law', named for a trans sex worker murdered in 2016 whose attacker was released after 48 hours despite footage and witnesses and has been on the run since): Mexico City is the second of the country's 32 states to criminalise transfeminicide - earlier in 2024 Nayarit, a small Pacific-coast state, introduced sentences of up to 60 years for the crime; the law also lets victims' friends, not only relatives, claim bodies and drive investigations, which matters where families disown trans relatives; it lands against more than 95% impunity for homicides in Mexico in 2022, believed higher for transfeminicides.

localsOnly: The unremedied adults-only gap in the recognition procedure is a resident documentation problem; visitors carry federally issued passports.
tangentialFactors: The lethality ranking comes from national hate-crime tallies that count all LGBT+ victims together - violence targeting gay men and lesbians forms part of the state's numbers.
